articles.title: Polls open across Manitoba for the 'wonderful opportunity' to vote in municipal elections
articles.summary: Municipal election day is underway across Manitoba. Voting locations are open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

image.caption: Manitobans will choose their next mayors, councillors and school trustees on Wednesday. (John Woods/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Manitoba
Municipal election day is underway across Manitoba. Voting locations are open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Eligible voters can cast ballots for mayors, councillors, school trustees
Manitobans are headed to the polls in municipal elections across most of the province.

Voting locations are open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. for casting ballots for mayors (or reeves, as the head of council is known in many rural municipalities), councillors and school trustees in the majority of Manitoba's 137 municipalities.

A general municipal election happens every four years and always on the third Wednesday in October. The only exceptions are in Winnipeg Beach, Dunnottar and Victoria Beach, where elections were held July 24.
"It's a great day to go out and exercise your right to vote," said Sherwood Armbruster, the City of Winnipeg's senior election official.
Results for all of Manitoba will be updated as they are received from voting locations on the 2026 Manitoba municipal elections website shortly after polls close at 8 p.m., .
CBC Manitoba will also have coverage of the election online and on radio and television.
Voters wait in line at Bison Run School for the polling station to open on Wednesday morning. (Meaghan Ketcheson/CBC)
Tyler Wiwchar was first in line to cast his ballot at Bison Run School in the Waverley West neighbourhood of south Winnipeg, stopping on his way to work.

"I thought the first stop would be coming to vote as it it's an important thing to do — try to get there as soon as possible," he said. "Everyone should be able to have the opportunity to come vote and select someone that represents Winnipeg."
His choice was still being determined as he waited for the door to open. As Wiwchar did some last second research, he used a sports analogy for making a selection.
"Yeah, just like a hockey decision, a quick and quick and simple play," he joked.
Bola Osagie says she believes the people she voted for 'are good candidates that would move this area forward.' (Rudy Gauer/CBC)
Bola Osagie, who made her choice right after Wiwchar at Bison Run School, called it a privelege to vote.
“It's a wonderful opportunity to express what I wanna see done in the city," she said.
"I listened to them talk and I found out about the people I wanted to vote for and I believe that they are good candidates that would move this area forward."
The City of Winnipeg says the busiest times at polling stations are typically right when the they open and then again from 3 p.m. until close.
Don’t worry if you're still waiting to vote at the deadline, Armbruster said. As long as you're in line, you'll be able to mark your choices.

"If you are attending during a peak period, thank you for coming and being patient and getting to know your neighbours and know that we are providing the service as quickly and accurately as absolutely possible," he said.
If you have the option, consider voting during the quieter period between 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., when the process may be a little quicker.
Winnipeg voters must be Canadian citizens, at least 18 years old on Oct. 28 and Winnipeg residents or property owners for at least six months (since April 28), the city says.
Eligibility to vote in municipal and school board elections can by found on the provincial government website. This includes eligibility for non-resident voters in municipal elections.
More choice
More Manitobans are getting a choice of who leads their communities than in 2022.
There are fewer acclamations compared to four years ago, the Association of Manitoba Municipalities said. Uncontested races are down to 30 per cent from 37 per cent in 2022.
At the same time, the number of women candidates has increased to 340 this year from 289 in the previous election, the association said.
Incumbent mayors in several Manitoba communities, however, were acclaimed after no challengers registered to run. Those include Portage la Prairie, Winkler and Niverville.

items: More Manitobans get a choice of candidates in this year's municipal election

blocks.text: Some places, like the Municipality of Cartwright-Roblin and the Rural Municipality of Argyle, saw their entire slate of council candidates acclaimed.

There's also more voting flexibility this year in Winnipeg, home to more than half the province's population. There are 184 polling stations and registered voters should have received a card letting them know exactly when and where to cast a ballot.
"The voters card is going to present not one, but two convenient locations," said Armbruster.

"We're also proud of the fact that we had a record number of advanced voters. More than 50,000 Winnipeggers have already cast their vote, which is 20 per cent higher than the previous record that was set four years ago."

items: Winnipeg, Brandon set early vote record as advance polls close

blocks.text: If someone hasn’t received a voters card, they can call 311 to ask where their polling station is, or look it up on the city's where do I vote? web page.
"We always recommend you bring your voters notice if you have one. If you don't, bring one piece of valid government-issued photo ID with your name and current address," said Armbruster.
A list of accepted ID is available on the city's website.
If you're not sure which ward you live in, you can check out a series of ward maps on the City of Winnipeg website. There's a set of school division ward boundary maps too.
With files from Meaghan Ketcheson

articles.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
articles.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

image.caption: A poster in Burkina Faso depicts the country's military leader Ibrahim Traore with the Russian president Vladimir PutinImage: Christina Peters/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The conflict with the West sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine prompted Russian President Vladimir Putin to seek support from other parts of the world. Africa has become a focus, with foreign minister Sergei Lavrov visiting the continent increasingly often.
Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova has described it as a "historic return," and declared no one and nothing could be compared to what Russia did for Africa in the 20th century.
Russia's most important African partner: Egypt

A Russia-Africa summit has been held in Russia at roughly three-year intervals since 2019. The third takes place in Moscow on October 28 and 29. The program focusses on economic cooperation. Other topics range from politics and security to science and culture. But Russia is actively working with only a few African countries, mainly in the north of the continent, and this is reflected in the trade figures.

"South Africa is still Africa's largest national economy, but its volume of trade with Russia is small, far less than with Egypt and Algeria," says Ivan Klyszcz from the International Centre for Defence and Security (ICDS) in Tallinn, Estonia.

"Egypt and Algeria in particular are key partners for Russia. Egypt plays an important role in this regard. Russian diplomats and business representatives are trying to extend relationships with other countries, especially Tanzania and Ethiopia, but with no appreciable success so far."

Egypt is the second-largest economy in Africa, and the bilateral volume of trade with Russia has more than doubled since 2021; in 2025, according to Russia's Federal Customs Service, it was $10.5 billion (€9.4 billion). Consignments of Russian grain are the main drivers, followed by products of the metal industry. Egypt's exports to Russia are primarily fruit and vegetables.

There are investment projects, too. Russia is building a big nuclear power plant in the Egyptian region of El-Dabaa on the Mediterranean coast. Construction is being financed by a Russian loan of 25 billion US dollars, which covers around 85% of the costs.

blocks.caption: Construction site of the Russian-financed El-Dabaa nuclear power plant in EgyptImage: SNA/IMAGO

blocks.text: Egypt is one of the few African countries with which Russia enjoys stable business relationships, as well as having extensive experience of cooperation, says Nikita Smagin, an expert on Russian policy in the Middle East. "In the long term, Egypt could become Moscow's gateway to Africa and to other markets," he says. "But Cairo is pursuing its own interests. It would be too optimistic to hope that Egypt is lending its support purely out of political solidarity."
Russia's economic role in Africa

According to the Russian customs service, around 39% of Russian–African trade in 2025 was with Egypt, and total sales between Russia and all 54 countries of the African continent came to around 27 billion US dollars. Africa's share of Russia's foreign trade is therefore very small (3.9% in 2025), and not at all commensurate with the attention Moscow is devoting to its relations with African countries.

Russia is not a significant trading partner for Africa, either. The most important partner for African countries is the European Union. In 2025, the volume of trade with the EU came to around 385 billion US dollars. African countries' statistics also show that other partners were well ahead of Russia. The volume of trade with China was in excess of 348 billion US dollars in 2025; with the United States it was almost 105 billion, and 103 billion with India.

Fidel Owusu, a Ghanaian expert with Geopolitical Intelligence Services (GIS) in Liechtenstein, comments that Russia's economic presence in Africa has not been as significant as that of China, the United States, India, or other traditional powers like France and Britain. "If you look at the volume of trade and the kind of investment," he says, "in recent times, some middle powers such as Turkey and the UAW are doing far better than Russia."

Beverly Ochieng, a senior analyst with Control Risks, a global risk and strategic intelligence consultancy in Senegal, observes: "Western countries continue to dominate in strategically important areas such as raw material extraction, finance, and the energy sector, even if their political presence in the region is declining." According to her, "Russia will compete more intensively for access to critical mineral resources and energy projects. We see this with lithium projects in Mali as well as with nuclear power initiatives across the continent."
Russian mercenaries in Africa

Russia's presence in Africa is more obvious in the military sector than in the fields of trade and investment. Starting with the arrival of the Wagner Group, Russian mercenaries have been supporting African regimes, particularly those of the unstable countries in the Sahel region. In exchange, their associated subsidiaries are granted access to raw materials. Following the death of the Wagner Group leader, Yevgeny Prigozhin, most of these operations were taken over by the Africa Corps, a paramilitary group set up and controlled by Russia's defense ministry.

According to the Congressional Research Service, the think tank of the US Congress, the largest Russian military contingents, each comprising several thousand men, are in the Central African Republic, Mali, and Libya. The Africa Corps is also keen to extend its presence in Burkina Faso and Niger. Russian mercenaries have also been spotted in Equatorial Guinea.
How Mali's big bet on Russia is backfiring

Irina Filatova from the University of Cape Town stresses that there are several reasons why it's important for Russia to maintain a military presence in Africa. "The countries have sizeable deposits of minerals such as gold and uranium. Through them, it's possible to exert influence over Europe's southern borders, including in matters of migration and regional security. With regard to Libya, the country is an important logistical hub for connections with the Sahel and central Africa. Goods can easily be supplied via Libya to countries without access to the sea," Filatova says.

Ultimately, Russia is still one of the biggest suppliers of arms to African countries, even though Russian exports have fallen over the course of the war in Ukraine. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimates Moscow's share of the African market for the years 2021–2025 at 15%, which puts it in third place behind the United States (19%) and China (17%). Between 2020 and 2024, its share was even higher: It was in first place with 21%, followed by China with 18%, and the US with 16%.
What are Russia's diplomatic aims in Africa?

Ivan Klyszcz from the ICDS says that while Russia is not a significant economic partner for Africa, the fact that it supplies food and fertilizer and has a military presence in some countries means that Moscow's influence in Africa is far greater than is suggested by the volume of trade and investment alone.

"I believe Russia sees the diplomatic weight of Africa," says Fidel Owusu. "When I talk of diplomatic weight, I mean numbers – the continent has the largest number of countries. Russia wants that kind of support in the UN General Assembly whenever votes are cast. In recent times it has done better than in earlier votes."
The perception of Russia in Africa
In recent years, Russia has been positioning itself on the international stage as representing the interests of the Global South.

"We want to work with Africa, we are working with Africa and we will continue to do so. But our aim is not, as it was for the colonial powers, to make money or steal something from Africa, but to develop together," Russian president Vladimir Putin said recently at a conference of the Moscow-based Valdai Discussion Club.

blocks.caption: Russian president Vladimir Putin referred to the colonization of Africa by European powers and said Russia would do things differently Image: Mikhail Metzel/Sputnik/REUTERS

blocks.text: References to the colonial past appeal to some countries but not others, says Irina Filatova. "Africa is not a country, it's a continent. There are differences in the perception of Russia, as well as in the way Russia positions itself. Also, the views of the political elites are often substantially different from those of ordinary citizens. In South Africa, for instance, the Russian narrative is received very positively. An anti-colonial agenda is also popular in other countries, but it isn't necessarily associated with Russia."
Antonio Cascais contributed to this report. It was originally written in Russian.

articles.title: Bernardo on saying Jinggoy got P573 million in kickbacks: It's hard to implicate a friend
articles.summary: State witness Roberto Bernardo said it wasn"t easy for him to implicate Senator Jinggoy Estrada, whom he accused of receiving P573 million worth of “commitments” or kickbacks.

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 5:46pm

State witness and former Public Works undersecretary Roberto Bernardo on Wednesday said it wasn’t easy for him to implicate Senator Jinggoy Estrada, whom he accused of receiving kickbacks from government projects.
Bernardo made the testimony when he was quizzed by Sandiganbayan Fifth Division justices and Estrada’s counsel, Laurence Arroyo, as to why he did not implicate Estrada in his September 2025.

Bernardo only later accused Estrada of receiving “commitments” of kickbacks from government infrastructure projects in November 2025 and in his latest October 26, 2026 judicial affidavit, which claimed the amount of kickbacks Estrada received reached P573 million.

“During that time [of my first affidavit], I have no confirmation, I have no solid evidence that will prove [his involvement]. I have already in [my] mind that he is a proponent [of projects], but I have to confirm [first],” Bernardo said.
“Ang hirap po ipahamak ang kaibigan. Hindi ko po agad magagawa iyon,” Bernardo added.
(It is tough to betray a friend. I cannot do that easily.)
Bernardo also pointed out that his previous affidavit, made prior to 2026, provides that given the complexities in the case, he reserved his right to “execute a supplemental affidavit if warranted.”
Bernardo also testified that the P573 million were delivered to Estrada in four installments: in November 2024, December 2024, February 2025, and June 2025.
Bernardo said he only personally delivered the commitments to Estrada in June 2025.
“It was June of 2025 when I delivered [it] with my driver,” he said.
“It was in multiples of P20 million [per sealed box] per report of Opulencia. Alam ko po na may ganoong halaga,” he said.
(I know that such is the amount.)
Gerard Opulencia is also a state witness like Bernardo and a former regional director of the Department of Public Works and Highways National Capital Region District Engineering Office.
Bernardo also said that Estrada asked for P1 billion project allocation under Senate leadership fund for election spending.
Bernardo told the anti-graft court what was indicated in his judicial affidavit wherein he said Estrada told him, “Tulungan mo na lang ako diyan kasi marami pa akong tutulungan sa eleksyon.”
(Kindly help me because I will be helping a lot of people during the 2025 elections).
Asked by the Sandiganbayan justices if the request was made in person, Bernardo said it was through a phone call.
“Tawag po,” Bernardo said.
When the court held a five-minute recess a few minutes after these statements by Bernardo, Estrada asked the Sandiganbayan to allow him to return to his cell in New Quezon City jail in Payatas.
Sought for comment, Estrada said he was satisfied with the cross-examination of his lawyers and that Bernardo’s testimony is inconsistent.
“Hindi naman siya nagdala ng pera sa akin,” Estrada said.
(He did not bring money to me.) — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot stake rival claims to lead Israel after deadlocked vote
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot offered competing claims to lead Israel after Tuesday's election, with Netanyahu calling for a right-wing government and Eisenkot saying…

blocks.text: World·New

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot offered competing claims to lead Israel after Tuesday's election, with Netanyahu calling for a right-wing government and Eisenkot saying voters had rejected the longtime Israeli leader, even as early counting showed no clear winner.
Voter turnout was 77.7%, Israel's Central Elections Committee said, the highest in more than 2 decades
No clear winner in pivotal Israeli election, exit polls suggest

Israel's Central Elections Committee was tallying votes on Wednesday and it will likely take until Thursday before definitive results of the election — the first since the Hamas-led attack of Oct. 7, 2023 — are known.

With some 48.4 per cent of votes tallied, Netanyahu's bloc was projected to win 55 seats, and Eisenkot's bloc 50 seats, with 15 seats going to Arab parties, Israeli media reported — a distribution will likely change as more votes are tallied.
That leaves both sides short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, and neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot claimed victory.

While the projected results may represent a setback for Netanyahu and his nationalist-religious coalition, a deadlock could work in his favour, leaving the 77-year-old in office as a caretaker prime minister during what are likely to be prolonged coalition negotiations or even until another election can be held.

An aide speaks to Likud Leader Benjamin Netanyahu as he gives a statement following exit polls for Israel's national election, at the party's election headquarters in Jerusalem early Wednesday. (Ammar Awad/Reuters)

Netanyahu's bloc ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, which themselves campaigned on a platform of bringing down the prime minister and his far-right allies. Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party and a former military chief, has all but ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, complicating his path to power.
Far-right religious parties led by Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich were projected to take a combined 13 seats within Netanyahu's bloc — with no major gains for either of them.

items: Israelis shatter turnout records in election that will pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu
Will Israeli voters turf Netanyahu?

blocks.text: Netanyahu, addressing party faithful after 3 a.m. local time at Likud election headquarters in Jerusalem, called for the formation of "a strong, right-wing national government."
Trump backed Netanyahu
He also highlighted Israel's military successes and raised the prospect of renewed joint action with U.S. President Donald Trump against Iran.

"Israel faces a singular historical opportunity, together with our partner President Trump, to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all. But ulterior motives must not divert us from this sacred mission," he said.
Trump, who endorsed Netanyahu, was asked early on Wednesday about the election after a campaign trip to Texas, and said he did very well.
Supporters of Gadi Eisenkot react after the release of the first exit poll results in Israel's general election in Tel Aviv on Tuesday. (Ariel Schalit/The Associated Press)

"You know, it's pretty close, which was very well. Because I think when the endorsement went out, it helped him a lot, but I actually heard he did pretty well. It might be winning or tie. The tie is sort of considered a win in that case because it's a big chess match."
Eisenkot said the public had voted against Netanyahu remaining prime minister and urged him to retire from politics, while warning against the use of Israel's security for political purposes.
High voter turnout

"Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people's trust," Eisenkot said, calling on the security establishment to "stand firm" against any attempt to put political interests ahead of Israel's security.
Voter turnout was 77.7 per cent, Israel's Central Elections Committee said, the highest in more than two decades and around seven percentage points higher than in 2022.

Israel's fragmented political system leaves smaller parties potential kingmakers in coalition negotiations that have run to weeks or months after past elections. If neither bloc can form a government, another vote may need to be held, something Eisenkot opposed given the high voter turnout.
No clear winner
If projections hold, Netanyahu's right-wing bloc, which at its height held 68 seats, would fall short of the 61 needed to govern, leaving him with no clear path to forming a government.

items: Netanyahu 'fighting for his political life' in 1st Israeli vote since Oct. 7. He might still survive
Netanyahu faces fresh allegations he ignored warnings about Oct. 7 — right before an election

blocks.text: Eisenkot, 66, who lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war, emerged as Netanyahu's strongest challenger, stressing his security credentials while positioning himself as a centrist domestically.
He entered politics only four years ago and joined Netanyahu's war cabinet after the 2023 Hamas attack, but quit eight months later, criticizing the prime minister's leadership.

A man walks past a Likud party campaign banner in Tel Aviv on Tuesday, featuring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump, with a Hebrew message reading, 'We have one opportunity to win.' (Baz Ratner/The Associated Press)

Eisenkot offers a break with Netanyahu's leadership and far-right allies, but not with the hawkish approach to security that has become more entrenched since the 2023 Hamas attack. He opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas' military wing must be destroyed or dismantled.
Eisenkot says Israel's response — a war that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza health authorities — was a failure because Hamas remains in charge.

Voters grappled with the trauma of Israel's deadliest day, when Hamas killed 1,200 people, according to Israeli government tallies, and took 251 hostage, and the wars in Gaza and with Lebanon's Hezbollah and Iran that followed.
While Netanyahu was criticized for the country's biggest security failure, he argued that he had made Israel and the world safer by killing top leaders of Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran.

articles.title: Ten reported dead after two trains collide in Spain – Europe live
articles.summary:
Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo

At least 10 people are feared dead and many more injured after two high-speed…

blocks.text: At least 10 feared dead after collision in Toledo province

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa
At least 10 people are feared dead and many more injured after two high-speed trains collided in Toledo province in central Spain.

Spain’s state rail infrastructure authority said services between Madrid and the southern region of Andalucía had been suspended “⁠following a rear-end collision between two trains” on Wednesday morning.
A spokesperson for the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha region, where the crash occurred, said the cause and ‌ number of injuries were yet to be determined.
Government sources told El País at least 10 people had been killed, and that the crash could be worse than the Adamuz rail disaster in January in which 46 people were killed.
We will bring you all updates here.
Key events

items: 15m agoDeath toll likely to rise, local government spokesperson warns
18m agoAt least 10 feared dead after collision in Toledo province

blocks.text: Today’s accident evokes grim echoes of last year’s tragedy in Adamuz, where 46 people killed and 152 were injured after two high-speed trains crashed in Adamuz, the province of Córdoba.

With almost 4,000km of track, Spain’s high-speed railway network ranks as the largest in Europe and the second biggest in the world after China, according to the Spanish infrastructure administrator Adif.

The network is tremendously popular, competitively priced and generally considered a safe mode of transport. In 2024, Renfe said more than 25 million passengers had travelled on its high-speed trains that year.

But in another major incident in 2013, 80 people died after a train derailed in the country’s north-west near Santiago de Compostela. An investigation concluded the train was travelling at 179km/h on a stretch of the line with an 80km/h speed limit when it left the tracks.
We are getting first pictures from the scene now…
Death toll likely to rise, local government spokesperson warns
Local government spokesperson told TVE that the death toll “will almost certainly rise.”
Esther Padilla told the broadcaster the situation “is going to worsen.”
She said the affected trains are likely to be Iryo 7076 with 146 passengers plus one baby on board, and AVE 2080 with 397 passengers on board, El País reported.

articles.title: Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official
articles.summary:
Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment

The “unprecedented”

blocks.text: The “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.

As the current outbreak reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths, Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.
“We want all countries to know that they are not safe if they don’t take appropriate measures,” he said.
“Each country, not only in the African region, but all continents, must now increase the preparedness level and the possibility for treatment.
“It is the first time three African regions have been affected [by Ebola]. The geographic extension of this outbreak is unprecedented,” he said.

blocks.caption: Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa CDC. Photograph: Ken Cedeno/Reuters

blocks.text: Kaseya said leaders around the world should realise that although the brunt of the health crisis is affecting Africa at the moment, the situation could change. “We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”
This outbreak, the 17th in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since Ebola was identified, was caused by the Bundibugyo virus and has become the largest and deadliest in the country’s history.

Ebola is a highly contagious, severe, and often fatal illness. It is spread through direct contact with body fluids such as the blood or vomit of infected people, or dead bodies, such as during funeral preparations.

On 15 May, DR Congo’s health ministry declared an outbreak in Ituri province, though sequencing shows it had begun in February. It has now spread to Kenya and Uganda in east Africa, while last week, in west Africa, Nigeria confirmed a case in the capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus.
France is the only non-African country to have confirmed a case of Ebola so far – a doctor who had returned from DR Congo – in June.

blocks.caption: Travellers at a hand-washing station in Busia on the Kenya-Uganda border, where health officials screen for Ebola symptoms, 12 October.  Photograph: Bright Emoja/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The Bundibugyo virus has no approved treatment, though vaccine trials are under way. The results should be available in three to six months, said Kaseya.
Of the total 10,091 cases, 10,060 have occurred in DR Congo, with 4,887 deaths. Two people have died in Uganda, and two in Kenya.

The response to the crisis has been hampered by inadequate protective equipment and unpaid health worker wages, leading to strikes. Conflict in DR Congo as well as mistrust towards officials in affected areas, misinformation and global aid cuts have further complicated the situation.

Kaseya will convene a meeting of African health ministers on Wednesday to urge greater cross-border cooperation. He wants governments to introduce screening and testing for people coming from affected regions at points of entry and exit.
“The main message to ministers is that they have to understand they could be affected, and we don’t want them to be surprised by what could happen,” he said.

blocks.caption: Red Cross staff simulate evacuating the remains of an Ebola victim in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, 22 October. Photograph: Tony Karumba/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: At a meeting in November with African heads of state, Kaseya will call for a “corridor of peace” in conflict areas. “Currently, we have colleagues in Ituri who want to go and support the population, but they cannot because of insecurity,” he said. “I have to say to leaders, this outbreak is not for rebels, it’s not for the official army, it’s for everyone. Ebola can affect everyone … We need to come together to have a kind of agreement on how to protect each other.”

Kaseya called for a global effort to fund the response. He said governments had pledged $3bn (£2.3bn), but that more than $2bn was still outstanding. African countries had committed $120m, he said, while the rest is meant to come from international donors including the US, the UK and the EU.

“We need this money now,” he said. “We must understand that failure to provide funding now to African countries [will result in more being spent] because the outbreak will continue to move. If we have other countries affected we’ll be talking about trillions of dollars because it will require a lot of support to stop this outbreak.”

articles.title: Spain train crash: at least 10 feared dead after collision in Toledo province
articles.summary:
High-speed service reportedly runs into back of another train, knocking two carriages off track

At least 10 people are feared dead and many more injured after two high-speed trains…

blocks.text: At least 10 people have died and many more are feared injured after two high-speed trains collided in Toledo province in central Spain.

Spain’s state rail infrastructure authority said services between Madrid and the southern region of Andalucía had been suspended “⁠following a rear-end collision between two trains” on Wednesday morning.

Esther Padilla, a spokesperson for the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha region, where the crash occurred, said authorities could confirm 10 deaths. “The information we are receiving is not good at all. There are at least 10 dead and it is possible that the number will increase,” Padilla told local media.
Government sources told El País that the crash could be worse than the Adamuz rail disaster in January in which 46 people were killed.

blocks.caption: Passengers check departure boards at Santa Justa station in Seville after the crash. Photograph: Europa Press News/Europa Press/Getty Images

blocks.text: Spain’s state broadcaster, TVE, reported that the crash happened after a high-speed train ran into the back of another service, knocking two carriages off the track.

Footage broadcast by regional Castilla La Mancha Television ​showed a derailed train with at least one carriage remaining on an elevated section of track. Twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line.
The rail operator Adif said the collision occurred on ⁠the line from Madrid to Seville.
Manuel Galán, the mayor ​of ​Urda near the ​city of Toledo, said he had ​been ‌asked by ​emergency ​services to prepare a sports hall to accommodate the injured.
Spain’s main political parties, which are gearing up for next month’s general election, suspended their planned activities for the day.

The prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, expressed his shock at news of the crash. “I remain in constant contact with the transport minister, and with the president of Castilla-La Mancha,” he said in a post on X. “Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations. My love, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families.”

The opposition People’s party leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, said on X: “Very concerned about the information we are getting about a new rail accident. The priority now is to attend to the victims and support their families. My full support to the emergency teams working on the ground.”

articles.title: DepEd: Classes suspended once heat index hits 42 degrees Celsius, but coordination with LGU needed
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) said a school can suspend both physical and online classes once the local temperature hits 42 degrees Celsius, upon coordination with the concerned local…

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 5:18pm

The Department of Education (DepEd) said a school can suspend both physical and online classes once the local temperature hits 42 degrees Celsius, upon coordination with the concerned local government unit (LGU).

The agency issued the statement amid the ongoing El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to bring record-breaking temperatures in the Philippines especially when it rises to a very strong or "super" phase late in the year.

In a media interview at Lakan Dula High School in Tondo, Manila, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said, "They (School officials) should just notify the LGU, part 'yun, required iyon kasi part of coordination iyon para hindi magulat si mayor or so governor na bakit nag-uuwian na 'yung mga bata."
(They should just notify the LGU, that's required as part of the coordination so that the mayor or governor would not be surprised that the kids are going home.)
DepEd has issued Memorandum No. 64 s. 2026, which sets comprehensive guidelines for schools during the El Niño.
Under the new memorandum, extreme heat will no longer trigger a blanket suspension nationwide.
School heads are instead expected to use a localized, decision-making tool that relies on indoor classroom temperature and humidity readings taken at 8 a.m., 12 noon, and 2 p.m.
According to the DepEd's new guidelines, there will be regular, face-to-face classes if the heat index is below 27 degrees Celsius.
When conditions rise to anywhere between degrees Celsius to 32 degrees Celsius, school heads can choose to shorten onsite hours or transition into hybrid learning.
Once the heat levels reach anywhere between 33 and 41 degrees Celsius, physical classes are suspended and learners will shift to home-based tasks.
If the heat level reaches 42 degrees Celsius and above, physical and home-based activities are completely suspended.
"We cannot afford to wait until extreme heat hits before we act. Our plan this year is proactive, deliberate, and organized," Angara said in a press statement.

"We are making sure our schools are fully prepared to manage heat stress, water shortages, and health risks, protecting the safety and well-being of our learners and personnel without unnecessarily sacrificing precious classroom time," he added. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Several people killed after high-speed trains collide in central Spain
articles.summary: At least 10 people have been killed in a train crash in central Spain, local authorities have confirmed. Rail services between Madrid and Seville have been suspended.

image.caption: Ten people have been killed in a train crash in Spain which has seen several such accidents in recent yearsImage: Juanma Jiménez/Europa Press/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: We have moved our coverage to a live updates. Please join us here.
At least 10 people were killed in a train crash in central Spain on Wednesday morning, local authorities have confirmed.
"The information we are receiving is not good at all," a spokeswoman for the government of the Castilla-La Mancha region told local media, giving an initial death toll of ten.

"There has been a collision between two trains [and] there are injured people," added Manuel Galans, mayor of the town of Urda in the province of Toledo, near to where the incident took place just after 9 a.m. local time.
The mayor of another nearby village, Jesus Perez of Los Yebenes, told Spanish TV that the accident appeared "serious."
Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia told local broadcaster TVE that it was a "high impact accident, it will be a major tragedy" but said it was too soon to confirm a final casualty figure.
"We don't just need help from nearby hospitals, we need nearby hospitals that have ICU beds," she added.
Spain train crash: what do we know?
The cause of the collision was not immediately known, but initial reports suggested one train had slammed into the back of another train which had been stationary.

"We heard a massive roar, a truly ​enormous thud ‌that went on for 10 seconds as if the train were about to derail," one passenger, Miguel, told local radio station COPE. "Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train – I imagine it must have been the other one."
Images from the scene showed at least two severely damaged train carriages flipped over on their side after tumbling down an embankment.

blocks.caption: Ten people have been killed in a train crash in Spain which has seen several such accidents in recent yearsImage: Juanma Jiménez/EUROPA PRESS/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: One of the trains, operated by AVE, was reportedly carrying 397 passengers while the other, operated by IRYO, had 146 people on board, according to the Castilla-La Mancha local government spokeswoman.
A reporter for local broadcaster TVE described scenes of "absolute chaos" and a constant stream of ambulances and emergency vehicles.
El Pais cited witnesses describing numerous injuries and ​arrival of emergency medical teams at the scene.

"All resources are currently being deployed," spokesperson for the Spanish emergency services told the AFP news agency, including "several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units."
In a post on social media, rail operator Adif confirmed that "traffic ​on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail line ​has been suspended following a rear-end collision ​between two trains."
Spanish PM Sanchez 'shocked' by 'serious' accident
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was "shocked" by the "serious" accident.

"Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations," he wrote on social media. "My affection, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families."
The collision comes just months after another devastating rail disaster near Adamuz in Andalusia in January.
In that accident, a high-speed train derailed and collided with an oncoming train, killing 46 people and injuring more than 150.
The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people. The January incident shook the confidence the European country has in its extensive high-speed rail network.

articles.title: Budget 2026 live: chancellor says scrapping of gas standing charges will save 60% of homes £45 a year
articles.summary: John Healey says UK faces ‘difficult moment’ as he prepares to deliver first budget of Andy Burnham’s government

blocks.text: Key events

items: nowGetting rid of standing charges on gas bills really 'sleight of hand', Tories claim
12m agoGreen party says 'business-as-usual budget' won't deliver hope
16m agoMoney saving expert Martin Lewis welcomes gas standing charge abolition, and says further energy bills support likely in budget
40m agoJohn Healey says chancellor scrapping gas standing charges will save 60% of homes £45 a year

blocks.text: Getting rid of standing charges on gas bills really 'sleight of hand', Tories claim

The Conservatives have dismissed the chancellor’s decision to get rid of standing charges from energy bills just “sleight of hand”. In an interview on GB News, Richard Fuller, the shadow chief secretary to the Treasury, said:

double quotation markWe know there’s a problem with energy prices coming down the track. That’s why the Conservatives last year actually announced that cheap energy plan to get rid of VAT on people’s energy bills and roll back some of the net zero taxes that burden people’s bills. But what Labour is doing is really sleight of hand. They’re moving it from one aspect of your energy bill or your taxes, and putting it somewhere else. Under the Conservatives, of course, we would make the tougher decisions on public spending, so the actual energy bills and people’s taxes would be coming down.

blocks.caption: Richard Fuller on Sky News Photograph: Sky News

blocks.text: Green party says 'business-as-usual budget' won't deliver hope
The Green party has put out this response to the news that gas standing charges will be abolished. A spokesperson said:

double quotation markAbolishing standing charges is more tinkering from a government that is failing to take the bold action needed to end the cost of living crisis. Energy bills have skyrocketed in recent years and are set to rise by hundreds of pounds again this winter. ‘Hope’ is an easy thing to promise but will not be delivered by a business-as-usual budget.
Money saving expert Martin Lewis welcomes gas standing charge abolition, and says further energy bills support likely in budget

John Healey found time to hold a meeting with Martin Lewis, the founder of MoneySavingExpert.com, in Downing Street this morning. Lewis is one of the most trusted voices on personal finance in Britain, and he has been campaigning for standing charges to be removed from gas bills for some time.

Speaking to the media afterwards, Lewis said Healey was in a good mood. He said he asked the chancellor if there would be a support scheme to help people with energy bills from January, when costs are set to rise sharply. Lewis said Healey would not confirm anything, but he said that “reading between the lines” he gathered that there will be an announcement on this. Lewis speculated that this could be an increase in the warm homes discount, or it could be help for people in lower council tax bands.
Lewis said:

double quotation markThe biggest issue in energy right now is that we’re expecting a 27% rise in the price cap in January. I asked the Chancellor whether he will be intervening on that. He told me I’d have to wait for the budget, but reading between the lines, yes, there will be an announcement today. Whether it’s an increase in the Warm Home Discount, or whether it’s council tax band, or whether it’s done via a payout for people in say council tax bands A-D as a proxy for household income as Rishi Sunak did who knows.

blocks.caption: John Healey saying goodbye to Martin Lewis after a meeting at No 11 this morning. Photograph: Neil Hall/EPA
A cleaner polishing the door this morning outside No 11, where John Healey will later pose for pre-budget pictures. Photograph: Thomas Krych/AP

blocks.text: John Healey says chancellor scrapping gas standing charges will save 60% of homes £45 a year

Good morning. When Andy Burnham became PM, he signalled that he wanted to end 40 years of neoliberalism. Judging by all the briefing about what will be in the budget today, neoliberalism is probably safe for another year or so because Burnham and his chancellor, John Healey, have decided not to use this as a moment for big, transformative change, but to instead opt for a more low-risk, every-little-bit-helps fiscal statement. There are radical elements in the Burnham agenda, but mostly they will have to wait for another day. In a video setting the scene for the budget, Healey sums it up with the slogan: “Breathing space today, and fresh hope for the future.”
Here is Pippa Crerar and Heather Stewart’s overnight splash story previewing the budget.
And here is an analysis by Phillip Inman setting out the main items we are expecting.

Every chancellor, though, likes to have at least one big surprise for the speech. This is the headline they want for tomorrow’s papers. We don’t know yet what Healey has chosen, but there is a lot of speculation that it will involve energy bills.
We have already had an announcement from the Treasury at 7am this morning about standing charges being removed from gas bills. Julia Kollewe has the story here.
According to the Treasury, this could save around 60% of families around £45 a year. It says:

The chancellor will announce today an end to this unfair and outdated practice. He will ask Ofgem to deliver removal of these charges – which are £108 a year for the typical household on average – in 2027 or as soon as possible after.
Instead, these fixed costs will be paid on the unit rate, which could save 60% of account-holding households around an average of £45 off their annual bill.

While this might sound like a modest cost of living measure – almost an “everyday fix” – Burnham and Healey – perhaps sensitive to the charge that there is not much radicalism in the budget – are presenting this as the start of something more ambitious. In a statement this morning, Burnham said this shows he’s “determined to reform our broken energy market” and Healey says:

My budget will draw a line in the sand on an energy policy that has failed British billpayers for years, letting extra costs on bills pile high and leaving households even more exposed to global shocks.

Healey is speaking at 12.30pm. We have also got PMQs today, but I will mostly be focusing on the budget, with reaction and analysis, and Graeme Wearden, who writes the Guardian’s business live blog, will be joining too to provide added firepower.
And we will also have comments open below the line (BTL).
Here is the agenda for the day.
8.45am: Andy Burnham chairs cabinet, where John Healey, the chancellor, will brief ministers on what’s in the budget.
Noon: Burnham faces Kemi Badenoch at PMQs.
12.30pm: Healey delivers the budget.
Around 1.30pm: After Healey finishes, Kemi Badenoch gives a speech responding to the budget. Other MPs respond as the budget debate continues through the afternoon.
2.30pm: Jonathan Haskel, chair of the Office for Budget Responsibility, holds a press conference.
3.30pm: Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, and Robert Jenrick, his Treasury spokesperson, hold a press conference to give their reaction to the budget.
If you want to get in touch, you can post a comment BTL and, if it’s addressed to Andrew, I may find it using a word search. But I am more likely to see it if you email politics.live@theguardian.com.

articles.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
articles.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

image.caption: Senegal is hoping to make Africa's historic moment count beyond the next two weeksImage: Fatma Esma Arslan Ozdel/Anadolu/IMAGO

blocks.text: On the final day of October, what may well be the final Summer Youth Olympics ever will begin. It will be the first on African soil as around 2,700 athletes aged 15-17 arrive in Senegal to compete across a total of 153 events in 25 sports.

Hosted in eight venues across three locations – Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly, 80 kilometers (50 miles) from the capital – these Games are seen by many as a prelude to Africa hosting a full Olympics one day in the future.
"I'm really excited about the Youth Olympic Games because, for the first time, I'll be representing our country," 15-year-old judoka Aisha Diop who is competing for Senegal told DW.

"I am very proud to be able to represent my country at these Games. This will really motivate young African athletes because they will improve, and they will want to continue playing sports now that the Youth Games have been held here."
Senegal gears up for Youth Olympic Games
An historic Games for Senegal and Africa
The 2026 Youth Games in Senegal will also be a first beyond the history it is making in Africa.
"Of the 2,700 athletes who will be competing in Dakar, there will be a 50-50 split between men and women," Olivia Nloga, Chief Brand Promotion Officer on the organizing committee, told DW.
"But this parity isn't just reflected in the overall figure. This gender parity will also be reflected in each event and in each sport where such parity actually exists."

Several sports are also making their debut at the Youth Olympic Games, such as five-a-side baseball, kung fu and the Senegalese specialty of beach wrestling. There's also a refugee team at the Youth Olympic Games for the first time.
"As I said earlier, the Youth Olympic Games aren't just about sports, and they aren't just about infrastructure," said Nloga.

"For us, it was also important to use this time to build on and reinforce the idea that these Games in Senegal are a celebration for the people. We did this by investing in culture—for example, through a fashion show and a program called Yi-sol, which is a mural project on the city's walls."
Rewriting the rules of African fashion
Other projects designed to celebrate the people include music, and a local student designed the mascot. The biggest focus of all though, is on creating sustainability for the young people of Senegal.
"We did so through a program that is very important to us – one that is close to our hearts, namely, the Olympic Civic and Sports Certificate," Nloga said.

"We traveled to schools throughout Senegal and worked with more than 1,000 instructors to reach and make an impact on more than one million young Senegalese children who, during this hiatus, were exposed to and educated about the values of the Olympic Movement."
With recent flooding in the country, there were concerns that infrastructure would have been affected, but Nloga insisted that flood risk had long been in the planning.

"The prime minister held an interdepartmental meeting during which he established a task force to ensure that the necessary arrangements and follow-up measures are put in place to safeguard both the competition venues and the accommodation sites."
Domestic issues remain

With Formula 1 confirming its return to Africa earlier in October, global sport is slowly becoming a more regular event in Africa. As a result though, there have been questions asked about the legacy of such events.

Many in Senegal concerned by the high cost of living and unemployment will see these Games as an unnecessary expense. For the Senegalese authorities though, they are an opportunity for long-term investment in the country's young people as well as infrastructure. There is also the hope that this will make Dakar a major tourist destination.
There was further criticism of the Games being in Senegal from Human Rights Watch (HRW), with the NGO calling on the Senegalese authorities to change their stance on the LGBTQ+ community.
"You are welcoming all of the world. It shouldn't be 'you are welcome to our country, except this, except that,'" Larissa Kojoué from HRW told DW.
"Anti-LGBT legislation and that crackdown that is going on, they contradict the Olympic movement, the Olympic Charter, and also various human rights convention that the country has signed."

Earlier this year, Senegal President Bassirou Diomaye Faye signed into law new legislation on same-sex relations that have proved contentious abroad despite broad political support within the majority Muslim country's parliament. Several human rights groups had voiced concerns about the bill, including warning that it would dissuade people at risk of illnesses like HIV/AIDS from seeking help.
Russia's return to the Olympics

The Games also see the return of Russians to Olympic competition under their own colours after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) lifted their suspension in July. Nevertheless, each sport's international federation can decide whether to authorize the Russian athletes' participation. World Athletics, for example, is upholding its ban, while judo and swimming have allowed Russians to return to competition with their flag and national anthem. According to the Russian Olympic Committee, 13 athletes will compete at the Youth Games in Senegal accompanied by 10 coaches.
Dakar's voice for cultural change
Despite the various concerns, there is an overriding hope that the Games will be prove beneficial for all involved.
"What makes the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar special is that they are also rooted in Senegal's extremely strong sporting culture," Nloga said.

"Every evening, when you take a stroll along the Corniche in Dakar, you're struck by the number of people you see exercising, regardless of their age or physical condition. What we'll be offering during these Olympic Games is also an immersion into Senegalese life – into the way sports are just as much a part of Senegalese identity."
Sira Thierij conducted interviews for this article. Edited by: Chuck Penfold

articles.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
articles.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert…

image.caption: An attack has occurred outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade Image: Armin Durgut/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A knife-wielding assailant attacked a police guard outside the Israeli Embassy in the Serbian capital, Belgrade, overnight to Wednesday, slightly wounding the officer before being shot dead by him, Serbia's interior minister said.
Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said the attacker, whom he described as a minor, had been monitored by security agencies as a supporter of the terrorist organization "Islamic State" (IS).

blocks.caption: The area around the embassy was secured by police after the attackImage: Serbian Interior Ministry/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Israel's Foreign Ministry later confirmed an "attempted terrorist attack" near its embassy in Belgrade, adding that no personnel were injured and the incident was being investigated.
What else we know about the Belgrade attack?
The attacker was thought to come from the western Serbian town of Sabac and "kept the black flag in support of the 'Islamic State' on his Instagram” account," according to the minister.
Dacic said the assailant shouted "Allahu Akbar," or "God is great" in Arabic, during the attack on the guard. According to Dacic, the guard killed the attacker in self-defense.
He said police were treating the incident as a terrorist attack, with the terrorism threat level raised to its highest, or "red alert."
"This means tighter security checks and an increased police presence at sensitive sites, including infrastructure facilities and places where large crowds gather," he said.
The attack came just days after key early parliamentary election in Serbia and one day after Israel held its parliamentary vote, with no clear result yet in sight.

blocks.caption: Police have raised the terror alert to its highest levelImage: Serbian Interior Ministry/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Previous Israeli Embassy attack in Belgrade
In June 2024, an attacker with a crossbow seriously wounded a Serbian police officer guarding the same embassy in Belgrade before being shot and killed by police.
That attacker was identified as a 25-year-old Islamic convert from a village near the capital who had become radicalized.

articles.title: What’s hindering us from progress in our power generation, transmission, and distribution segments?
articles.summary: Top energy leaders tackle the Philippines’ energy crisis in this roundtable discussion

blocks.text: Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by AboitizPower and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

With high electricity prices, vulnerable infrastructure, and critical supply, it can be difficult for Filipinos to have an optimistic outlook not only for our energy industry’s future, but also even just for the present. Did you know that in the Visayas alone, there have been nearly 130 yellow and red alerts since January 2026?

“Nagkakaroon tayo ng red and yellow alerts. Maraming kadahilahan. Maaaring kinapos ang supply, may mga planta na nasira, o kaya naman ay may mga planta na nasa construction nga pero na-delay din ang pasok,” said Atty. Francis Saturnino “Nino” Juan, chairperson and CEO of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC).

(We have red and yellow alerts. There are many reasons behind this. It may be from a lack of supply, broken power plants, or probably power plants that are under construction but got delayed in deployment.)

Juan said this in the panel discussion “Energy for Progress: Strengthening the Vital Links of our Energy System”, where he was joined by Energy Secretary Sharon Garin and Prof. Rowaldo “Wali” Del Mundo, who is the associate dean of the College of Engineering in the University of the Philippines (UP) and the UP System’s vice president for development.
Moderating them was Ruth Yu-Owen, the energy committee chairperson of the ECCP (European Chamber of Commerce).
“Energy for Progress” is part of Rappler’s “Powering Up” roundtable discussion, done in partnership with Aboitiz Power Corporation and the ECCP.

There is a perfect fuel mix fit for the Philippines, according to Energy Secretary Garin, but notes that it is an “evolving formula” that contains a mix of renewable energy, as well as baseload (steady and more affordable, like coal) and mid-merit sources that can fill up the gaps left by variable and intermittent supply.

“The technologies change faster than our policies, so we keep catching up. And now what we’ve done is do a super simulation to have some projections, get a super computer with super people from DOE and the rest of the industry so we can calculate what to expect in the next 10 years,” quipped Garin.
There’s also a need to create new regulations and even revisit the Philippine Grid Code, Juan added, on account of new technologies coming into the grid.

“Nakapaloob kasi din diyan ’yung [energy] reserve requirements natin, so tinitingnan kung ano na ba ’yung sufficient na reserve. Anong klase na ’yung reserve na dapat papasok? So ito ang mga sinosolusyunan natin ngayon.”

(It also houses our [energy] reserve requirements, so we get to check what kind of reserve is sufficient. What kind of reserve should we integrate? So these are the things we are trying to solve right now.)

Meanwhile, Del Mundo stressed the need to catch up on project delays, especially as demand for electricity continues to grow. It can be recalled that the Department of Energy has been calling out projects that failed to meet their development commitments.
“Electricity supply interruptions send ripple effects to other sectors of the economy, and this ultimately leads to economic losses,” the Philippine Institute for Development Studies said.

In terms of alleviating the cost of power, Del Mundo also emphasized the importance of strategic procurement on the part of distribution utilities for both the short-term and the long-term, with the latter serving as more of a signal for power producers to build more future capacity.
But even then, Del Mundo observed that there were long-term contracts that didn’t result in new capacity.

Instead, these were crafted for existing power plants, making it uncertain that there is available capacity in the long run. Del Mundo said that there’s too much dependence on the existing power plants, suggesting the need for more alignment when it comes to procurement in the distribution sector.

During the first episode, Garin also highlighted Filipino innovation as a big anchor in building more energy capacity – like through agrivoltaics, or growing vegetables under solar panels, to balance out the demand of both for arable land.

Some forms of makeshift solutions have also come out of the Philippines being a climate-vulnerable nation, like what Garin recalled during her visit to a location that experiences floods: The people raised the pole mount of the solar panels.
The Philippines itself, as an archipelago, invites the need for innovation and exploration.

“Because of this, very expensive [and weak] ang ating transmission[…] So kung ang ating power generation ay magiging embedded, ibig sabihin, distributed… Bawat island, may adequate supply[…] so yung ating interconnection ay hindi natin kailangan problemahin na, “Kailan natin i-u-pgrade [o] lalakihan?” Ibig sabihin, importanteng ma-interconnect natin para ma-hold lahat nung mga island together para sa stable na operation,” Del Mundo said.

(Because of this, our transmission is very expensive and weak. So if our power generation will be embedded, meaning distributed… Each island, there’s an adequate supply, so we don’t need to stress about our interconnection in terms of, “When do we need to upgrade or expand?” This means it’s important to interconnect so the islands will be held together for a stable operation.)
Electric cooperatives should also be improved in terms of their capacity-building and infrastructure, Garin said.
The far-flung areas served by these cooperatives shouldn’t be forgotten, the panel maintained, with Juan adding that the consumers’ best interest should always come first.
For Del Mundo, an option could be combining multiple electric cooperatives into just one entity per region to produce scale and, ideally, improve overall performance and power rates.

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 4:41pm

Retired police major general Mao Aplasca, former acting Senate sergeant-at-arms, on Wednesday filed his counter-affidavit with the Department of Justice (DOJ) in connection with a direct assault complaint over the May 13 Senate shooting incident.
“He submitted his counter-affidavit today,” Justice spokesperson Polo Martinez said in an ambush interview.
The complaint was filed by the Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG).
According to Martinez, the PNP-CIDG is given until November 6 to file its reply affidavit.

“So option po ‘yun sa PNP-CIDG. They don’t have to, but they can. And if they do file their reply affidavit, then the respondents, Mao Apalsca as well as two other respondents forming part of the OSAA, will also then have the chance to file their rejoinder affidavit,” he said.
Martinez said that if the PNP-CIDG will not file a reply affidavit on November 6, the complaint will be submitted for resolution.

To recall, Aplasca fired warning shots on May 13 while the upper chamber was on lockdown, sending Senate personnel, media practitioners, and other civilians inside the Senate premises into panic and chaos.
In July, the Ombudsman ordered the dismissal of Aplasca because of grave misconduct and gross neglect of duty over the shooting incident. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: US War Secretary Pete Hegseth proposes US-ASEAN defense cooperation framework
articles.summary: United States Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Wednesday proposed developing a framework for defense cooperation between America and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) ahead of the…

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 4:30pm

United States Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Wednesday proposed developing a framework for defense cooperation between America and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) ahead of the 50th anniversary of relations between Washington and the regional bloc in 2027.
Hegseth made the proposal during the ASEAN-United States Defense Ministers' (ADMM) Informal Meeting in Cebu.
"Next year marks the 50th anniversary formally of US-ASEAN relations, an important milestone," Hegseth said.

"In recognition of this milestone, we propose that we work together to develop a US-ASEAN framework for defense cooperation, a practical framework that guides our cooperation over the next several years," he added.
Hegseth said Washington is ready to begin working on the proposed framework with Singapore as the latter assumes the chairmanship of the ADMM-Plus.
'Peace through strength'
According to Hegseth, the US wanted to strengthen cooperation with ASEAN members particularly in maritime domain awareness, military interoperability, and naval cooperation.
Hegseth stressed the US commitment to a more stable, secure, and prosperous Indo-Pacific.
"Strong enough to deter coercion and aggression. Quiet enough to avoid needless escalation or public theatrics and to let our actions speak for themselves," he said.

"But clear enough that our friends, our partners, and potential adversaries understand precisely where the United States stands and that we will defend our interests and the interests of our allies and partners. That is, by definition, peace through strength," he added.

For Hegseth, the strategy is intended to deter coercion and aggression while avoiding unnecessary escalation and clearly communicating the US position to its allies, partners, and potential adversaries.

"We're not going to agree on everything, nor do we need to. But an agreement on the fundamentals is enough to support practical cooperation where our shared interests are overlapping and are clear," Hegseth said.
Engagement with US

Meanwhile, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto "Gibo" Teodoro Jr. welcomed continued US engagement in Southeast Asia and expressed appreciation for Washington's support for ASEAN centrality and ASEAN-led mechanisms.

"We value the United States' sustained engagement. With the defense establishments of ASEAN as a robust US presence is necessary for peace and stability in Southeast Asia and in the broader Indo-Pacific region," he said.
Teodoro cited existing cooperation in maritime security, military medicine, cybersecurity, and humanitarian assistance and disaster response.
He said these initiatives provided opportunities to strengthen partnerships in support of regional peace and stability and a free and open Indo-Pacific.
The Philippines is hosting the 20th ASEAN Defense Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) and the 13th ADMM-Plus on October 28 and 29 in Cebu.
ADMM is ASEAN's highest defense consultative and cooperative mechanism, according to the Department of National Defense (DND).
The ADMM-Plus expands defense cooperation to eight dialogue partners, including Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia, and the United States.
The South China Sea and the West Philippine Sea are expected to be among the topics discussed during the meetings. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Kenyan family protest extradition hearing delay of ex-British soldier accused of murdering kin
articles.summary: No official reason has been given for postponing next month’s hearing to May 2027, family says.

blocks.text: The family of a Kenyan woman allegedly murdered by a British soldier 14 years ago has expressed outrage after an extradition hearing for the accused was postponed until May 2027.

Relatives of Agnes Wanjiru, whose body was found in a septic tank near a British army training camp in Kenya in 2012, described the delay as "completely unacceptable" and accused authorities of failing to keep them informed.

The hearing for Robert James Purkiss, a former British soldier accused of killing the 21-year-old mother, had been due next month. The family said it had now been postponed until May 2027. Purkiss was arrested in the UK last November and is fighting extradition to Kenya to face trial for murder. He denies the allegation.
Wanjiru's niece, Esther Njoki, told the BBC that the family learnt of the postponement through the UK embassy and had received no official explanation.
"We have exercised patience and endured uncertainty for years, but our patience is now being taken advantage of," she said in a statement.

"Agnes deserves justice. Her daughter Stacy deserves answers about what happened. And as a family, we deserve to be treated with dignity and kept informed about proceedings that profoundly affect our lives."
The family said it had already raised money and made arrangements to travel to the UK for the hearing, which was due to take place in three weeks.
It is now calling on the authorities to expedite the proceedings, warning that the latest postponement means the case will enter its 15th year without a trial.
The family said a UK court is expected next week to give the reasons for the hearing delay.
Wanjiru disappeared in March 2012 after spending an evening at a hotel in Nanyuki, about 200km (124 miles) north of Nairobi, where British soldiers were stationed for training.
Her body was found nearly three months later in a septic tank at the hotel. She had suffered stab wounds to her chest and abdomen and left behind a five-month-old daughter.
A Kenyan inquest concluded in 2019 that she had been unlawfully killed by one or two British soldiers.
In September 2025, a Kenyan High Court issued an arrest warrant for a British national after prosecutors presented evidence they said justified bringing murder charges.
Purkiss' lawyers said he intended to contest extradition to Kenya.
The 38-year-old former soldier appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court in February via video link, where he was further remanded in custody.
Last year, the then British Defence Secretary John Healey met Wanjiru's family during a visit to Kenya and pledged his government's support for efforts to secure justice.
The UK government has previously said it remains committed to helping the family, but would not comment on ongoing legal proceedings.

articles.title: Dela Rosa again presses SC to reverse ruling on ICC arrest warrant
articles.summary: Dela Rosa’s camp says the 'armed and dangerous' tag and P50-million bounty for his arrest place his right to life in 'present and serious danger'

blocks.text: BATO. Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa during the Senate plenary session on May 13, 2026.
Dela Rosa’s camp says the 'armed and dangerous' tag and P50-million bounty for his arrest place his right to life in 'present and serious danger'

items: Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa is urging the Supreme Court to reverse its ruling and halt the enforcement of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against him, citing escalating threats to his safety.
His lawyer argues that recent government declarations labeling him as 'armed and dangerous' and the offer of a ₱50-million bounty for his arrest place his life in serious danger.

The ICC issued a warrant against Dela Rosa due to his involvement in the controversial anti-drug campaign during former President Duterte's administration, which has been linked to thousands of deaths.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa has again pressed the Supreme Court to reverse its earlier ruling and stop the use of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against him.

In a manifestation on Tuesday, October 27, Israelito Torreon, dela Rosa’s lawyer, asked the SC to urgently rule on a pending motion for reconsideration they filed in June, seeking to reverse a May court decision that denied their plea for a temporary restraining order or a status quo ante order to stop the implementation of the ICC arrest warrant.
A status quo ante order simply means a rewind or the court wants things returned to how they were before a disputed action happened, while it decides the case.

Dela Rosa’s lawyer argued that the enforcement posture surrounding the senator had “escalated” while the motion remained unresolved. It cited supervening events, including the Department of the Interior and Local Government’s (DILG) declaration of the senator as “armed and dangerous” and the P50-million bounty offered for his arrest.

“Taken together, these are not stray remarks of individual officials. They constitute an announced executive enforcement program: an official ‘armed and dangerous’ designation, a ₱50-million capture bounty from public funds, a dedicated task force, Special Action Force deployment, and express presidential support, all directed at the arrest of a sitting senator of the Republic for surrender to a foreign tribunal, while the legality of that very act is pending before this Honorable Court,” the manifestation reads.
Voting 9-5-1, the SC previously denied Dela Rosa’s request for a TRO, saying he had “no clear and unmistakable right to be protected.”
The tribunal also noted that the Senate had provided the lawmaker with protective custody, preventing his arrest and the implementation of the ICC warrant.
“Hence, Senator Dela Rosa’s claimed invasion of his purported rights is more imagined than real,” the SC said.
Dela Rosa’s camp said the recent pronouncements from the executive branch placed the senator’s right to life in “present and serious danger.”

“No court has found Petitioner Dela Rosa to be armed and dangerous. In law enforcement practice, the designation signals to operating units that armed resistance should be anticipated, which is precisely the setting in which lethal force is most likely to be used,” it said.

“Coupled with a bounty and a declaration abandoning restraint, the designation places Petitioner dela Rosa’s right to life under Article III, Section 1 of the Constitution in present and serious danger,” the lawyer added.
ICC drug war case
The ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued a warrant against Dela Rosa in November last year due to his role in former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war.
He was Duterte’s first police chief who implemented the bloody anti-drug campaign which human rights organizations said took the lives of nearly 30,000 people.

The ICC named him a co-perpetrator in the case. It added that those involved “controlled a structure of power” which enabled them to “direct and control the actions” of those who carried out drug war killings.

In November, the ICC warrant was still sealed. It was only made public on May 11, after Dela Rosa, following months of absence in the Senate, showed up to back Senator Alan Peter Cayetano’s election as Senate president. For three days, Dela Rosa sought refuge inside the Senate building until a shooting chaos, which was allegedly triggered by his mistah, Senate sergeant-at-arms Mao Aplasca, ensued on the night of May 13. Hours later, Dela Rosa escaped from the Senate at around 2:30 am. He was accompanied by his political ally, Senator Robin Padilla.
Dela Rosa has since stayed out of public view. – with reports from Jairo Bolledo/Rappler.com
